findings.title: Bound file reads before rejecting oversized source or rollback data
findings.reasoning: _read_regular checks regular-file mode but calls handle.read() with no byte limit and no descriptor-size check. load_snapshot reads all six files before _verify_snapshot checks their exact lengths. A wrong or grown regular file can therefore allocate arbitrarily more memory than the fixed 905307-byte snapshot before PIN_MISMATCH. Rollback also fully reads caller-selected historical payload/manifest files before comparing them with deterministic expected bytes, so an altered oversized bundle has the same issue. Existing tests reject wrong lengths after allocation and do not cover the read bound.
findings.reproduction: IR-P01 uses an owned disposable six-file source, with first file exactly780684bytes and all remaining expected lengths, and a pass-through os.fdopen observer. Every handle.read call received -1. Total905308bytes were read before PIN_MISMATCH. IR-P02 replaces an owned disposable bundle payload with33954bytes when the deterministic payload is33953bytes; rollback read(-1) returned33954 before PUBLICATION_FAILED. Neither probe used a large allocation or changed protected source.
findings.recommended_correction: Require explicit finite limits for regular-file reads. Validate descriptor file size before allocation, use a bounded read such as limit+1 to catch growth after the size check, and retain exact post-read length/hash validation. Source limits come from immutable PINS. Bound candidate readback, rollback payload and rollback manifest using deterministic expected lengths or another justified fixed finite bound. Add negative read-spy/oversize/growth tests preserving the previous pointer and source bytes. Avoid relying solely on path.stat before reopening.
